title: Faster lanes, same quality (2x goal)
goal: Make a lane at least 2x faster than 0.5.4 on a fixed benchmark (bench/fixture notes API, 3 steps, loopback contract check), with the same quality gate: lane done, VERDICT ready, contract check green when rerun outside the lane.
now: Wave 2 running: checksvc + reviewfix lanes in parallel. Baseline 0.5.4 = 19.7 min median to a ready verdict (target <= 9.9 min).

waves.note: baseline showed review = 72% of lane time and every run needed a whole fix lane

Release 0.6.0 with ship.mjs --push, install on this machine

decisions.text: Measured the last plans: lead tail after the lane up to 60 min, serial review 4 to 20 min, rate-limit waits 27 min with 3 lanes.

Lane transcripts: model time 73% of build; CodeArts sandbox blocks loopback so worker check runs hang (3 min each) and workers fight SANDBOX_* vars; reviewers rerun the checks too. Targets: check service, review without reruns, thinking-off builder (thinking: disabled verified to reach MaaS).
Merged stepwait and stepreview with 2+3 reviewer findings fixed by the lead (resume baselines, findings only to builder sessions).

Bench v2 baseline on 0.5.4: 19.7 min median (16.3, 23.2), 2/2 needed one fix lane. Phases: review 184-752 s per lane vs build 75-212 s; reviewers spent minutes debugging the sandbox (no loopback, node -v hung 2 min). Sandbox network policy is a global CodeArts setting: not changed by the runner. Review templates now say: no local network, judge by reading.

risks: Thinking off may cost quality: only switch the default if bench quality holds
Model latency varies by hour: compare runs taken close together, 2 runs each
